Six years ago, in the wake of the devastating loss of 76 veterans at the Holyoke Soldiers’ Home during the COVID-19 pandemic, I stood outside the home with families and advocates like Paul Barabani, where we pledged to build a home befitting our servicemen and women. After years of advocacy and work at all levels of our government, we celebrated the fulfillment of that promise.

I want to thank the Healey-Driscoll Administration for their stick-to-itiveness, time and again delivering on projects that once seemed unattainable. I also want to thank the former VA Secretary Denis McDonough, whom I spoke with on numerous occasions leading up to the award of $263.5 million from the federal government. I made clear the urgency of this project and the need to prioritize its funding. He assured me he would do everything he could to expedite the delivery of these funds, and needless to say, he delivered.

While this was a day of celebration, it was also a day of solemn reflection, as we remembered those veterans who tragically lost their lives and did not have the chance to see this new home. No words or actions will ever undo that tragedy or erase the grief endured by their families. But through that tragedy came a renewed commitment to ensuring something like that would never happen again. This new home is a testament to that commitment and a lasting tribute to those we lost.
